title: Lewis, 'The atom and the molecule' (1916): cubical atom and the eight-electron shell
summary: In a Journal of the American Chemical Society article of April 1916, Gilbert N. Lewis published a theory of atomic structure in which the atom tends to hold eight electrons in its outer shell, normally arranged at the eight corners of a cube. He used that picture to treat the difference between polar and nonpolar compounds.
body: Gilbert N. Lewis published "The atom and the molecule" in the Journal of the American Chemical Society in April 1916. Lewis wrote that he had employed a theory of atomic structure for a number of years in interpreting chemical phenomena but had not previously published it, and that he presented it in this paper. Among its postulates: the atom has an inner kernel of positive charge and an outer shell whose electrons may vary between zero and eight in chemical change; and the atom tends to hold an even number of electrons, especially eight, normally arranged symmetrically at the eight corners of a cube. He applied the theory to the distinction between polar and nonpolar compounds, stating that the differing properties he tabulated are all due to a single cause. The article records receipt on January 26, 1916.
